Abysmal Service at a “MasterChef” Restaurant
May 2026 • Friends
Disappointing Experience – Long Wait, Left Hungry

Visited with friends from Singapore, Malaysia, and Germany during a conference stay nearby. Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing.

We ordered simple dishes (mushrooms, beef with vegetables, fried chicken, juice), but after 30 minutes there was still no food. When we asked, there was no clear response. We requested white rice first and were told they had run out, yet later they served just one bowl of white rice, which two of us had to share.

We agreed to fried rice instead, but it also never arrived and we eventually cancelled it.

For a place branded “MasterChef,” the service and execution were abysmal.

Regrettable, especially as this was our only night out during a 3-day conference.

Dreadful food & service
Jan 2019 • Family
The atmosphere was non existent, the service was patchy and the food a waste of money. Yes it is cheap eating but the reality does not match the expectation set by the menu. 
We had Spaghetti with Australia beef which I’m told by my dining companion was ‘alright’ but the beef was tough and literally cut into pieces the size of a pumpkin seed. 
The vermicelli noodles with crab meat seem to be missing the crab meat and was generally tasteless and clumpy. 
The place smelled like alcohol but there was none on the menu. 
Clearly the place up stairs that people were coming in to use the lift to get to was much more popular than our restaurant. 

Overall dreadful, give this place a miss! There are so many other places very close by.

A Kinda Satisfied Diner
Apr 2018 • Solo
This restaurant is on the ground floor of the Quarter Centre Hotel. Its signage identifies it as the Garden Master Chef Restaurant and Cafe. Its history is that the owner was Master Chef in VN a few years ago and has capitalized on that distinction by opening this restaurant. 
I had the broccoli cauliflower soup that presented as a green puree, served with croutons. It was unimpressive, as was the vegetable pakora dish served with standard tartar sauce. What was good was the “bún chả” (i think) that was the dish President Obama had. It was served with pork patties, a spring roll, noodles, a vinegary fish sauce sauce and fresh greens that were a bit ragged.
Service was at a snail’s pace for me and others too. It was busy while I was there. The place had a good ambiance and decor with soft music playing that was overwhelmed by the traffic noise outside. I was sitting near the entrance so that was to be expected.
Total cost of my meal was 250k VND.
